items.title: The Tonight screen hedges about a fact it knows: "may be below your horizon or your location is not set"
items.summary: Confirmed real. tonightSuggestionsProvider (target_suggestion_provider.dart:100-104) returns an EMPTY list the moment latitude==0 && longitude==0 — before it looks at the sky — so oneTapTargetProvider hands the screen a null pick and the card blamed the horizon, the moon and the location at once, offering only a Refresh that can never succeed. The null-pick branch is now _NoPickCard, which reads the same appSettingsProvider the dashboard/planner/weather surfaces read: unset site -> 'Location not configured' + an 'Open Settings' button routed to /settings?section=location; configured site -> the honest 'Nothing imageable right now' with Refresh kept. The GO path had the same hedge (the controller's NoTonightTargetException default): the screen's pick seam now checks the site itself and throws a message that names it, and the exception's default text was narrowed to the genuinely ambiguous case.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/tonight/tonight_no_pick_cause_test.dart :: 'no pick with an unset location names the location' (asserts the title, the Open Settings button, and the ABSENCE of the hedge + dead-end Refresh) and 'no pick with a configured location keeps the sky explanation' (guards against inverting it into always-blame-the-location). tonight_morning_report_state_test.dart needed a ProviderScope because the card now reads settings; both its cases still pass.
items.revert_check: Deleted the `if (locationUnset) { return _NoTargetCard(... 'Location not configured' ...); }` block from _NoPickCard.build (tonight_screen.dart). Result: 'no pick with an unset location names the location' FAILED — `Found 0 widgets with text "Location not configured"`. Restored; all 10 tests in test/screens/tonight/ pass.

items.title: "Unattended Autopilot" panel title is permanently truncated
items.summary: Confirmed real at the cited file, and the first fix for it was INCOMPLETE — I found the residual by measuring instead of trusting. The title was a single ellipsized Text inside a Flexible sharing a Row with the Idle/Running badge, so it rendered 'Unattended Aut…'. An earlier pass changed it to maxLines: 2 and proved that at a 1280 px window, where the panel is 358 px wide. But the panel width is clamp(available * 0.28, 280, 380), so every window from the desktop breakpoint (768) up to ~1170 px puts it on its 280 px FLOOR, and there the Row leaves the title exactly 100.0 logical px (measured: RenderParagraph constraints 0<=w<=100.0, didExceedMaxLines TRUE at text scale 1.0) — less than the word 'Unattended' needs, so two lines were not enough either and the title still clipped, now mid-word and without even an ellipsis. Fixed at the cause the finding itself named: the badge no longer competes for the title's line. The header Row is now Icon + Expanded(Wrap[title, badge]), so the badge stays beside the title while there is room and drops to its own run when there is not, handing the title the panel's full width (measured 214.6 px, didExceedMaxLines false). maxLines: 2 is kept with an explicit TextOverflow.ellipsis, because Flutter's default with maxLines set is TextOverflow.clip — a mid-glyph cut with no cue — which is the wrong way to fail at a very large system text scale.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planner/widgets/scheduler_tab_content_test.dart :: 'the autopilot panel title fits at the narrowest panel width, with the status badge dropping to its own line to make room' — pumps the real SchedulerTabContent at 1050x900 (the widest window that still sits on the 280 px panel floor, chosen so the assertions cannot be disturbed by the queue table beside it) in the Running state (the widest badge), and asserts RENDERED geometry: the title's RenderParagraph.didExceedMaxLines is false, and the badge's top is at or below the title's bottom, i.e. the Wrap actually broke the run. The pre-existing 1280 px case ('queue header, decision panel, and Target queue render') is kept and still asserts didExceedMaxLines is false there.
items.revert_check: Restored the original single Row (Flexible title + SizedBox + badge, maxLines: 2, no overflow) in decision_panel.dart. Result: the new test FAILED with 'Expected: false / Actual: <true> / the autopilot panel title is clipped at the 280 px panel floor'. Restored from a byte copy; all 10 tests in scheduler_tab_content_test.dart pass and dart analyze is clean on both files.
items.caveats: Independently re-verified in this pass, not taken on trust — the earlier maxLines-only fix passed its own test and was still wrong at every window below ~1170 px.

items.title: The Object types dialog reflows when a chip is selected, sliding Apply down under the pointer
items.summary: Confirmed real. The 7 FilterChips sit in a Wrap; Material's default leading checkmark widened the selected chip by 20 logical px, which pushed the Wrap from 2 rows to 3 and moved the Clear/Apply row down. Set showCheckmark: false — selection is already carried by the chip's fill and outline, so the chip is the same width in both states and the action row cannot move. The dialog body was extracted to _showObjectTypeDialog + a @visibleForTesting seam (same pattern as the existing showAngleSliderForTest) because PlannerScreen runs a 1 s sky clock and never settles.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planner/object_type_dialog_stable_layout_test.dart :: 2 cases asserting RENDERED geometry — the Nebula chip's Rect and the Apply button's Rect are byte-identical before and after selection, and all 7 chips plus Apply keep their rects when the whole set is selected.
items.revert_check: Removed the `showCheckmark: false` line. Result: both cases FAILED with the exact defect — `Expected Rect.fromLTRB(384.6, 227.0, 503.2, 275.0) Actual Rect.fromLTRB(384.6, 227.0, 523.2, 275.0)` (the chip grew 20 px). Restored; both pass.

items.title: Constellation filter is an unsearchable list of 3-letter abbreviations
items.summary: Confirmed real: _ConstellationDropdown built a DropdownButton with one row per constellation present in tonight's candidates, each labelled 'Constellation: <Abbr>'. Replaced with a _ControlChip that opens a searchable dialog (consistent with every other filter in that row): rows read 'Canes Venatici (CVn)', sorted by full name, with a search field that matches either spelling, a live count of how many constellations tonight's candidates actually cover, and an explicit 'Any constellation' action. The abbreviation->name table was a PRIVATE map inside skotiq_planetarium's OpenNGC catalog; it is now the shared constellation_names.dart (constellationFullName()) and catalog.dart delegates to it, so there is one spelling of 'Canes Venatici' in the app. The finding's ask for 'only constellations with candidates tonight' was already true (availableConstellationsProvider derives from the suggestion set).
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planner/constellation_filter_picker_test.dart :: 4 cases — rows render 'Canes Venatici (CVn)' and no 'Constellation: And' prefix; typing 'ursa' narrows to Ursa Major and picking it returns the abbreviation 'UMa' the filter speaks; typing 'cvn' matches the abbreviation; 'Any constellation' returns the clear sentinel (distinct from a barrier dismiss, which must be a no-op).
items.revert_check: Changed the row label back to 'Constellation: $abbr'. Result: 3 of 4 cases FAILED (full-name row not found, search-by-name found nothing to tap, abbreviation search matched nothing). Restored; all 4 pass.

items.title: The Rationale block never names the target it is explaining (and calls a target with no frames a "large unfinished dataset")
items.summary: Both halves confirmed real. (1) session_optimizer_service.dart:527 gated the line on `primary.dataProgress < 0.25`, and dataProgress is EXACTLY 0.0 when nothing has been captured (target_suggestion_service._calculateDataProgress returns 0.1 for the 'some data, no plan' case), so a target with zero frames was sold as a 'large unfinished dataset' and an 'efficient completion target' in the same block that said 'No data collected yet'. Now gated on `> 0 && < 0.25` and reworded to 'Partially captured already...'. (2) The Rationale SectionHeader read 'Why this plan was chosen' while the numbers under it always belong to plan.primaryTarget — which is NOT the hero card whenever a search or filter leaves a different card on screen. The subtitle now names the target ('Why NGC 6015 was chosen'). I did NOT move the block above the candidate list: that is a layout preference, not a truth defect.
items.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/session_optimizer_service_test.dart :: 'a target with no frames is not called an unfinished dataset' + 'a partially captured target still gets the completion rationale' (the pair pins BOTH directions so the fix cannot be 'delete the line'). packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planner/planner_rationale_names_target_test.dart :: 'the Rationale section names the target it explains' — pumps the real PlannerScreen with one seeded suggestion and asserts 'Why NGC 6015 was chosen' is present and the generic subtitle is gone.
items.revert_check: (1) Restored `if (primary.dataProgress < 0.25) 'Large unfinished dataset makes this an efficient completion target.'`: BOTH core cases FAILED. Restored; 18/18 pass. (2) Restored `subtitle: l10n.text('plannerRationaleSubtitle')`: the app case FAILED — `Found 0 widgets with text "Why NGC 6015 was chosen"`. Restored; passes.

items.title: Getting a target into the scheduler is a three-deep dead end; every empty state points at another empty state
items.summary: The dead end is real and I reproduced it in the code: the Add Target sheet (project_dialogs.dart) was a picker over `allDbTargetsProvider` ONLY, and with an empty library it rendered 'No targets in the catalog / Add targets to your library first' with no action — while the only writer of the targets table reachable from the UI was Framing -> Save target (framing_provider.saveTarget) and the plan-tonight sequencer helper. The sheet now also searches the installed sky catalogs (new `installedCatalogSearchProvider` in core — the existing plannerInstalledCatalogSearchProvider deliberately HIDES tonight's candidates, which is exactly backwards for adding one) and creates the library row itself via TargetLibraryService.ensureCatalogTarget (host-aware and dedup-safe), then returns the new id so the caller attaches it to the open project. Rows already in the library are filtered out of the catalog section so an object never appears twice, the row shows type/mag/constellation, and an in-flight add disables the list so a double tap cannot double-create. The empty state now says what to do ('Search for an object by name or catalog id') instead of pointing elsewhere.
items.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/planner/add_target_can_add_test.dart :: 'an empty library can still add a catalog target and attach it' — pumps the real ProjectsTabContent with an EMPTY allDbTargetsProvider (the exact dead-end state), opens Add Target, types M31, taps the catalog row, and asserts the library was asked to create it (name, catalogId, RA converted deg->hours, Dec) AND that the project service attached the returned id to the open project.
items.revert_check: Deleted the `if (newFromCatalog.isNotEmpty) ...` section from the sheet's list (the catalog half). Result: the test FAILED — `Found 0 widgets with text "Not in your targets yet"`. Restored; it passes, and the pre-existing projects_tab_content_test.dart (10 cases) still passes.

items.title: Scheduler moon avoidance is illumination-only; the app has moon separation everywhere else
items.summary: Confirmed: TargetConstraintKind had timeWindow / moonIlluminationMax / customHorizon / scheduledWindow and nothing separation-based, so the wizard's 'Moon avoidance' step offered exactly one knob whose semantics are backwards for the common cases (rejects a target 150 deg from a 90% moon, accepts one 10 deg from a 40% moon). Added `moonSeparationMin` end to end: enum + `moonSeparationMinDeg` field + payload encode/decode (payload_json, so no schema migration) + engine evaluation in the same hard-constraint loop as the others, reusing the engine's existing Meeus moon ephemeris and angular-separation helper, with a rejection reason that states the actual separation and the moon's phase. UI: a new 'Moon separation' wizard card + 0-180 deg field + review sentence + row label, and the illumination card was renamed from the over-broad 'Moon avoidance' to 'Moon illumination' now that the pair exists. Default 30 deg. NOT done and left as a decision: the illumination-scaled Lorentzian curve (NINA's) and the missing min-altitude / max-airmass / meridian-side kinds — see the needs-decision item below.
items.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/scheduler/moon_separation_constraint_test.dart :: 5 cases against the real engine at a fixed clock where the moon's position is computed independently (RA 22.70 h, Dec -13.76): a 79-deg-high target 131.7 deg from the moon is rejected by a 150 deg gate (and by NOTHING else — rejectionReasons.length == 1), passes a 60 deg gate, a target sitting on the moon is rejected by a modest 30 deg gate, a disabled constraint is not evaluated, and the payload survives the storage round-trip. packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/scheduler/widgets/target_constraints_editor_test.dart :: 'the wizard can build a moon SEPARATION constraint, not only an illumination cap' drives the 3-step wizard against a real drift DB and reads the row back.
items.revert_check: Replaced the engine's `case TargetConstraintKind.moonSeparationMin:` body with a bare `break;` (constraint stored but never evaluated — the exact shape of a placebo fix). Result: 2 of the 5 core cases FAILED (`Expected: true Actual: <false>` on the rejection assertions). Restored; 84/84 core scheduler tests and 18/18 app scheduler tests pass.

items.title: The Night Outlook ranks by geometry alone: a mag-13.2, 1.9-arcmin galaxy outranks M31 and M27
items.summary: Half-confirmed, and the correction matters. target_scoring.dart's composite is altitude + moon + transit + darkness + airmass — all geometry, no magnitude, no size. BUT the finding's 'nothing accounts for whether it fits the sensor' is not the whole truth: target_suggestion_service.dart:204-212 already blends in a framing-fit term when an equipment profile yields an FOV — at weight 0.08 against terms that sum to ~1, i.e. worth at most ~7 points on the 0-100 badge. That is why NGC 6015 and IC 1231 still tie at 76 above M31 at 64: the framing term exists but is too weak to move anything, and with no profile at all it is absent. Also: the two rankers 'disagreeing' is by design and documented in the code — the Recommendation tab's banner is a read-only preview of the SchedulerEngine's pick, and the card list below it is the whole-night OUTLOOK. Changing the default ranking changes what the app recommends on its headline screen, which is a product call, and a second agent is actively rewriting this area (packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/tonight_ranking.dart appeared mid-session), so implementing it here would collide.
items.options: (a) Raise the existing framing-fit weight from 0.08 to something decisive (~0.25-0.35) and add a mild surface-brightness/magnitude term, so a 30-arcsec planetary at 1.29"/px cannot top the list — costs nothing new, but it re-ranks every user's Plan Tonight overnight and makes the outlook depend on having an equipment profile. (b) Leave the score as pure observability and instead default the Size filter to the FOV-fitting range whenever a profile exists (the app knows the FOV the moment one is saved) — reversible with one click, visible to the user, and leaves the score meaning 'how well-placed', which is what its factor names promise. (c) Leave both and add a 'Fits your rig' sort mode.
items.recommendation: (b), plus a modest bump of the framing weight to ~0.15. Ranking by observability is defensible and the score's own breakdown chips claim exactly that; silently folding 'is it worth imaging' into the same number makes the badge unexplainable. A defaulted-but-visible Size filter fixes what the operator actually complains about (unimageable specks at the top) without inventing an opinion inside a number labelled altitude/moon/transit.

items.title: Two different score scales for "how good is this target tonight" on the same screen
items.summary: Confirmed. Plan Tonight > Recommendation renders TargetSuggestion.totalScore on a 0-100 badge; Plan Tonight > Schedule renders the engine's TargetScore.totalScore as a raw weighted sum with 3 decimals (target_score_row.dart:117), and the decision panel prints the same raw number again ('Score 1.655', decision_panel.dart:199). They are different algorithms over different inputs, and nothing on either surface says so or gives either number a unit. Both are only meaningful as a RANKING, which is a display decision rather than a defect in the maths — and the two candidate fixes pull in opposite directions, so I did not pick one.
items.options: (a) Normalise the engine score to 0-100 for display (divide by the sum of the configured weights, which is exact and already available on the decision). Both surfaces then read 0-100 — but they would look directly comparable while still being different metrics, which risks INVERTING the confusion into a false equivalence. (b) Leave the number and label the column 'Weight' with a tooltip that breaks out the per-factor contributions (the engine already ships them: the rejected-candidate rows render exactly that breakdown today). Honest and cheap, but it is disclosure, not a cure.
items.recommendation: (b) with the breakdown promoted from a tooltip to the row's expanded state — the same treatment 'Other candidates considered' already gives rejected rows — and rename the column header to 'Weight'. Two 0-100 numbers that disagree about the same object on adjacent tabs would be worse at 2am than one number that is openly a different, explainable thing.

items.title: "Run unattended all night" arms all-night automation on one click with no confirmation or readiness summary
items.summary: Confirmed: the Run button calls straight through to engine start / backend controlScheduler('start') with no dialog and no pre-flight summary (verified in scheduler_tab_content_test.dart, which taps the button and asserts the host call happens immediately). Whether the app's most automated action should ask first is exactly the kind of decision that defines the product: this is the ASIAIR-style one-button promise on one side and the NINA/SGP explicit-sequence discipline on the other. Stop/Pause and the Idle/Running/countdown states were already truthful, so nothing here is lying — it is a friction question.
items.options: (a) Add a confirmation sheet gated on a readiness checklist (weather safety, guider, park-at-dawn, disk space, first target) with a 'Start anyway' for the amber rows. Safer, matches NINA/SGP, and reuses the checklist onboarding already links to — but it puts a modal in front of the feature the product is sold on, every night, including the nights everything is fine. (b) Keep one click and render the same readiness rows INLINE in the panel above the button, so the state is visible before the click without gating it. (c) Confirm only when a row is amber/red (nothing warns on a healthy rig).
items.recommendation: (c). It preserves the one-click promise on a rig that is actually ready and interposes exactly when the click would have been a mistake — which is the only case the confirmation was ever for. If the owner wants a single rule instead, (b) is the honest one: show the state, do not nag.

items.title: "Alt now" is the wrong axis for a tonight planner
items.summary: Confirmed as described: the chip is 'Alt now', the sheet is titled 'Minimum altitude right now', and suggestion_filter_provider.dart:440-443 filters on visibility.currentAltitude — so used in daylight it culls by an altitude none of those objects will have tonight. The label is honest, though, and the filter is genuinely the right one for someone at the eyepiece deciding what to point at NOW. Changing which axis the planner filters on by default changes what Plan Tonight is for, and every suggestion already carries visibility.peakAltitude, so either option is cheap.
items.options: (a) Repoint the existing chip at peakAltitude and rename it 'Min peak altitude tonight', dropping the right-now filter. One chip, matches the whole-night framing of the rest of the tab — but it silently changes the meaning of a filter existing users may have set, and removes the at-the-eyepiece use. (b) Add a SECOND chip ('Peak altitude tonight') beside it and leave 'Alt now' alone. Nothing breaks, both questions are answerable — at the cost of another control in an already busy filter row and two similar-sounding chips to tell apart.
items.recommendation: (b), with the new peak-altitude chip placed first so it reads as the default question a tonight planner answers. The filter row already has 7 controls and wraps cleanly, and an operator who set 'Alt now' deliberately should not have it redefined under them.

items.title: The whole screens/suggestions/ UI ships but is unreachable from any screen
items.summary: Confirmed unreachable, with one correction to the finding: TransientAlertsPanel is NOT reference-free — packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/transients/alert_state_across_surfaces_test.dart:91,105 pumps it directly. So the state is 2,475 lines across 6 files (SuggestionFilters + its 3 control parts, ScoreBreakdown, TransientAlertsPanel) with zero production mount points and two tests that keep them green. The filter controls are superseded: the running app uses the planner's own _SortDropdown/_ResetChip/_ControlChip in planner_screen_parts/_filter_controls.dart. TransientAlertsPanel is different in kind — it is a real feature (tonight's transient alerts in the planning flow) that exists only under Analytics > Science today. Deleting it and mounting it are both changes to what the product offers, so I did not choose.
items.options: (a) Delete the whole directory and retire suggestion_filters_remote_test.dart — the honest end state if the planner's own controls are the answer, and it removes 2.5k lines of UI that no reviewer can reach. (b) Delete the filter/breakdown widgets but mount TransientAlertsPanel on the Plan Tonight > Recommendation tab, which is where an observer would expect 'a nova went off tonight' to appear and where it can actually change what they image. (c) Keep everything as a staging area for a future Suggestions screen (status quo: dead code that ships in every build).
items.recommendation: (b). ScoreBreakdown and SuggestionFilters are duplicates of shipped controls and should go; the transient panel is the one piece with a real user story, and Analytics > Science is the wrong place for something that is only actionable before the night starts. If the owner does not want transients on the planner, then (a) — (c) is the only option that is definitely wrong.

items.title: The scheduler still has no per-target minimum-altitude, maximum-airmass or meridian-side constraint
items.summary: Carried over from the moon-avoidance finding, whose second sentence — 'The wizard also has no minimum-altitude / maximum-airmass / meridian-side constraint, which are the three most-used per-target constraints in NINA and SGP' — was acknowledged when moonSeparationMin landed but never actually tracked anywhere. Re-confirmed against the tree: TargetConstraintKind is timeWindow / moonIlluminationMax / moonSeparationMin / customHorizon / scheduledWindow. Minimum altitude exists only as a SITE-WIDE SchedulerConfig.minAltitude (the slider in the decision panel's Scoring weights), or per-target by authoring a whole horizon profile and attaching it via customHorizon — which is a workable but heavy way to say 'never image this one below 35 degrees'. Maximum airmass and meridian side cannot be expressed at all, so 'east side only, flip is not worth it for this target' is not sayable. This is a feature-surface decision, not a truth defect: nothing lies, the constraints simply do not exist, and adding constraint kinds enlarges what the scheduler promises.
items.options: (a) Add altitudeMin (degrees) and airmassMax as first-class kinds — cheap and symmetric with moonSeparationMin (payload_json, no migration; the engine already computes altitude for the site-wide gate), and it makes the per-target editor match what a NINA or SGP user arrives expecting. (b) Add only altitudeMin, on the grounds that airmass is a monotone function of altitude and two knobs for one axis is how schedulers get confusing. (c) Add nothing and document that customHorizon is the per-target altitude mechanism — no new surface, but the wizard then has to explain a horizon profile to someone who wanted one number, and meridian side stays unsayable.
items.recommendation: (a) for altitudeMin, (b)'s reasoning for airmass — i.e. ship altitudeMin and let the field offer airmass as an alternate UNIT on the same constraint rather than a separate kind, so there is one axis with two spellings. Meridian side is the one I would hold back for a separate decision: it interacts with the flip logic and the scheduled-window bypass, so it is not a drop-in the way an altitude floor is.
